risk_register.description: Inconsistent or unsupported Markdown syntax (e.g., GFM, CommonMark, proprietary extensions) leads to incorrect or broken rendering of content in the final HTML. Relates to Q6.
Ambiguous or unsupported internal linking conventions (e.g., [[wikilinks]] vs. relative file paths) cause backlink generation to fail or be incomplete. Relates to A2, Q1.
The system fails to parse tags due to undefined conventions (e.g., YAML frontmatter vs. inline #hashtags), resulting in an incomplete or non-functional tag-based navigation system. Relates to A3, Q2.

The build process fails, crashes, or becomes unacceptably slow when processing a large number of notes or very large individual note files, making the tool unusable at the user's required scale. Relates to Q3.
Malformed YAML frontmatter in one or more Markdown files causes the build process to fail, either for the specific file or for the entire site.

A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists if raw HTML or script tags within Markdown notes are rendered without proper sanitization, allowing malicious content to execute in the user's browser.
The client-side search index becomes too large for large note collections, leading to slow page loads, high memory consumption, and a poor user experience for the search feature. Relates to A4, Q3.

Sensitive or private information contained within notes is inadvertently published to a public web server because access control is an explicit non-goal, and the user may not be fully aware of the public nature of the output. Relates to non-goal #3.
The generated site is not mobile-responsive or has poor usability on small screens, limiting its utility for users who access notes on mobile devices.
File name or note title collisions (e.g., 'index.md' in multiple subdirectories mapping to the same output path) cause pages to be overwritten or links to resolve incorrectly.
Circular dependencies between notes (e.g., Note A links to Note B, and Note B links back to Note A) cause a stack overflow or infinite loop during the backlink generation process.
The tool fails to handle non-UTF-8 character encodings in source files, leading to garbled text in the output or build failures.
Broken internal links are not handled gracefully (e.g., they crash the entire build instead of generating a warning and rendering as plain text). Relates to Q8.
Generated links use absolute paths that do not work correctly when the site is hosted in a subdirectory of a domain. Relates to Q5.
The Command Line Interface (CLI) tool has complex installation steps or a confusing user interface, creating a high barrier to entry for non-technical users. Relates to Q10.
The generated website has poor accessibility (e.g., insufficient color contrast, missing ARIA attributes, non-semantic HTML), making it difficult for users with disabilities to navigate.

If an incremental build feature is implemented, it may fail to detect all dependencies (e.g., changes to a shared template), resulting in a partially updated, stale, or inconsistent site. Relates to Q7.
The system does not support a wide-enough range of platforms (e.g., Windows, macOS, Linux), limiting adoption by the target user.

when_to_interrupt: Any build process failure (e.g., crash, non-zero exit code).
Validation stage detects a high number of broken links or accessibility violations above a defined threshold.
Build time or memory usage exceeds performance targets for the specified note scale.
